Recent employment listings for community and social services roles in Cheyenne, Wyoming, outline a broad spectrum of opportunities across local government agencies, healthcare providers, non-profit organizations, and federal contractors. Publicly available job boards reflect ongoing recruitment spanning behavioral health, social work, caregiving, and administrative support within Laramie County.

Overview of Available Roles and Employers

The listings feature various organizations seeking personnel for specialized positions. Notable roles and employers include:

  • Housing Coordinator & Skills Trainer: VOA Northern Rockies (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Employment Services Specialist & Benefits and Eligibility Specialist I: State of Wyoming (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Youth Alternatives Family Counselor & Police Victim Assistance Coordinator: City of Cheyenne (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Child Military and Family Life Counselor & MFLC Counselor: Leidos (F.E. Warren AFB / Cheyenne, WY)
  • Juvenile Services Crisis Care Worker & Inmate Program Coordinator: Laramie County Government (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Mental Health Therapist: Aspire365 and Reliatus Behavioral Health (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Licensed Clinical Social Work (LCSW) - Hospice: Enhabit Home Health & Hospice (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Personal Financial Counselor: Magellan Health and Magellan Federal (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Nursing Assistant & RN Staff: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Cheyenne, WY)
  • Interim Chief Executive Officer: Wyoming Business Council (Cheyenne, WY)

Practical Implications and Analysis

Job seekers navigating the Cheyenne labor market in community and social services will find a heavy concentration of behavioral health, counseling, and eldercare positions. Organizations ranging from local municipal departments to large federal contractors like Leidos and the Department of Veterans Affairs frequently post targeted openings reflecting regional service demands in healthcare and social support.

However, prospective applicants must carefully review individual listings for precise qualifications, as requirements vary significantly by position—ranging from entry-level caregiving to specialized clinical licenses such as LCSW, LMFT, LPC, or LAT.
